records.subject: Make-up examination due to medical reasons (mid-semester)
records.facts: Third-year student missed the mid-semester examination in CS-302 and CS-353 after hospitalisation for acute appendicitis. Institute Medical Officer endorsed the discharge summary. Application on Form BP-10 was filed within seven days of the last scheduled examination, with Form BP-12 for 8 days of medical leave.
records.discussion_summary: Clause 6.2.4 permits a make-up examination coordinated by the Department. Clause 8.3 allows medical leave up to 15 days in a semester on DUGC recommendation and HoD approval. Attendance in both courses remained above 75% after the leave.
records.resolution: Resolved that B.Tech./CSE/2022/118 be permitted to appear in the make-up examination for CS-302 and CS-353 as per Clause 6.2.4, and that 8 days of medical leave be recorded under Clause 8.3 on Form BP-12. Course coordinators shall conduct the make-up as per the guidelines of the office of the Dean (Academic).

records.subject: Attendance shortage below 75% - request for condonation
records.facts: Final-year student recorded 68% attendance in EC-412 after a documented medical episode spanning 12 days. Medical certificate from a Government hospital was endorsed by the Institute Medical Officer. The student requested extraordinary attendance relaxation under Clause 9.1 read with Section 8.
records.deficiencies: Attendance in EC-412 is 68%, below the 75% threshold of Clause 9.1. Without extraordinary relaxation the student would be awarded F grade and debarred from the end-semester examination.
records.discussion_summary: Clause 9.1 states that a student shall not be allowed to appear in the end-semester examination if attendance falls below 75% and shall be awarded F grade. However, as per Section 8, extraordinary attendance relaxation may be allowed; the student remains responsible for all other academic requirements. Medical leave of 12 days is within the 15-day cumulative cap of Clause 8.3.
records.resolution: Resolved that extraordinary attendance relaxation under Clause 9.1 read with Section 8 be recommended for B.Tech./ECE/2021/067 in EC-412 only, subject to fulfilment of all remaining academic requirements. The student shall not be debarred from the end-semester examination of EC-412.

records.subject: Semester drop / semester leave on medical grounds
records.facts: Student requested semester leave for Odd Semester 2023-24 following orthopaedic surgery. Treating hospital recommended 10 weeks of rest, exceeding the 15-day medical-leave cap of Clause 8.3. Form BP-12 was submitted with supporting documents.
records.deficiencies: Requested absence exceeds the 15-day cumulative medical-leave limit in a given semester under Clause 8.3.
records.discussion_summary: Clause 8.3 requires that medical leave longer than 15 days must convert to Semester Leave / Semester Drop, accepted by DUGC and SUGC. Clause 8.4 limits such semester leave to two semesters during the entire programme, with or without a break. This is the student's first semester leave. The student may appear in Grade Improvement Examination / Summer Semester to avoid academic loss.
records.resolution: Resolved that semester leave for Odd Semester 2023-24 be recommended for B.Tech./ME/2021/044 under Clauses 8.3 and 8.4, to be forwarded to Chairperson SUGC / Dean (Academic). The student may register for Grade Improvement Examination / Summer Semester as appropriate.

records.subject: Branch sliding / branch change after first year
records.facts: Student admitted in Civil Engineering in 2023-24 applied for branch sliding to Computer Science and Engineering after first year. First-year SPI/CPI and Institute sliding guidelines were placed before DUGC for noting. Three CSE-specific first-year courses (aggregate 9 credits) would remain to be earned after sliding.
records.discussion_summary: Clause 5.4 permits branch sliding based on first-year academic performance, subject to Institute guidelines. Credits of previous-branch specific courses do not count toward the new branch. The student must earn additional credits for left-out branch-specific courses of the allotted branch.
records.resolution: Resolved that the branch-sliding application of B.Tech./CE/2023/091 be forwarded as per Clause 5.4 and the Institute sliding guidelines. If allotted CSE, the student shall earn the additional first-year CSE-specific credits before becoming eligible for the B.Tech. degree.

records.subject: Credit transfer for industrial internship / online courses under MoU

records.deficiencies: One MOOC certificate did not state percentage marks required for Clause 6.3.2 grade equivalence.

records.resolution: Resolved that credit mapping for the internship and the complete MOOC be recommended under Clauses 6.2.6 and 6.3.2. The incomplete certificate shall be resubmitted with percentage marks before tabulation. The recommendation shall be forwarded to SUGC.

records.subject: Academic Deficiency (ACD) and Grade Improvement Examination
records.facts: Student obtained SPI 3.7 in Even Semester 2023-24 with one F grade in PI-204, meeting the definition of Academic Deficiency under Clause 7.1. Application on Form BP-11 sought Grade Improvement Examination in three courses.
records.deficiencies: SPI below 4.0 and an F grade in a registered course; student is ACD.
records.discussion_summary: Clause 7.1 categorises a student as ACD if SPI/CPI is below 4.0 or if ABS/N/F/X exists in any registered course. Clause 6.2.5 permits ACD students to appear in Grade Improvement Examination with a combination of F, X, ABS and N grades, maximum five courses, with prescribed fee on Form BP-11.
records.resolution: Resolved that B.Tech./PI/2022/073 be permitted to register for Grade Improvement Examination in the three applied courses under Clause 6.2.5, subject to payment of the prescribed fee. Academic performance requirements for the award of degree remain unaltered.

records.subject: Appeal against termination for Academic Deficiency
records.facts: Student was terminated after continued ACD and failure to meet minimum performance requirements. Appeal on Form BP-11b cited prolonged illness in 2022-23 and attached medical records. This is the first appeal.
records.deficiencies: Prior SPI/CPI remained below the Clause 7.1 thresholds; termination was processed under Clause 7.4.
records.discussion_summary: Clause 7.5 permits appeal against termination. Chairperson Senate shall not entertain any further appeal unless substantial additional information is brought to notice. An appeal shall not be entertained more than twice from the same student.
records.resolution: Resolved that the appeal of B.Tech./CE/2020/088 be forwarded to Chairperson SUGC / Chairperson Senate under Clause 7.5 with DUGC remarks, without a departmental recommendation on the merits, pending verification of the medical records by the Institute Medical Officer.
